findings.explanation: Every resource in the module sets encryption_spec.kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name, and HLD_GCP_172/205/226/228/229/403 confirm each one is wired to google_kms_crypto_key.vertexai. But setting kms_key_name only tells Vertex AI which key to use — it doesn't grant access to it. GCP requires the AI Platform service agent (service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key before any of these six resources can actually be created; nothing in this repo grants that. This is exactly the same companion-grant gap holden already checks for on other GCP CMEK integrations in this fleet (HLD_GCP_453 Cloud SQL, HLD_GCP_456 GCS, HLD_GCP_458 Pub/Sub, HLD_GCP_469 Workflows, HLD_GCP_474 Filestore, HLD_GCP_476 Document AI, HLD_GCP_482 Healthcare, HLD_GCP_485 Composer) — every one of those has a `requires_companion` rule for the service-agent grant, but no equivalent exists yet for any of Vertex AI's 24 CMEK-checked resource types (see suggested_policies). Deterministic engine can't see this because it only checks the attribute is non-null on the resource itself, not that a companion IAM binding exists elsewhere in the graph. Blast radius: every `terraform apply` of this module against a real project fails at resource-creation time with a Cloud KMS permission-denied error, on all six resources, until the grant is added by hand — which risks someone "fixing" it by dropping the encryption_spec block instead of adding the grant.
findings.title: CMEK is wired to all six Vertex AI resources but the Vertex AI service agent is never granted access to the key

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_172 requires google_vertex_ai_dataset.encryption_spec.kms_key_name to be set, but nothing checks that the AI Platform service agent actually has permission to use that key. Same gap class as HLD_GCP_453 (Cloud SQL) / HLD_GCP_476 (Document AI), applied to the dataset resource. coverage_by_type[google_vertex_ai_dataset] currently contains only HLD_GCP_172 (encryption presence), no companion-grant check.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Vertex AI datasets using CMEK must grant the AI Platform service agent key access
principle: key-management
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  Setting encryption_spec.kms_key_name on a google_vertex_ai_dataset does not
  by itself grant the AI Platform service agent permission to use the key.
  GCP requires the AI Platform service agent
  (service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to
  hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the referenced key, via
  a separate IAM binding that Terraform never creates automatically. Without
  it, dataset creation fails at apply time with a permission-denied error.
remediation: |
  Grant the AI Platform service agent access to the key:

    resource "google_project_service_identity" "vertexai" {
      provider = google-beta
      service  = "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
    }

    resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "vertexai" {
      crypto_key_id = google_kms_crypto_key.main.id
      role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
      member        = "serviceAccount:${google_project_service_identity.vertexai.email}"
    }
resources:
  google_vertex_ai_dataset:
    filter:
      path: encryption_spec.kms_key_name
      not_null: true
    any:
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
          linked_via:
            from: encryption_spec.kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding
          linked_via:
            from: encryption_spec.kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

suggested_policies.rationale: Ordering counterpart to the dataset grant-existence policy above, same shape as HLD_GCP_465 (Cloud SQL) / HLD_GCP_494 (Document AI): the grant and the dataset both reference the same key without either referencing the other, so Terraform can create the dataset before the IAM grant propagates.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Vertex AI dataset CMEK grant must be depended on for correct provisioning order
principle: key-management
severity: HIGH
message: "google_vertex_ai_dataset with CMEK must declare depends_on on the KMS IAM grant to guarantee correct provisioning order"
rationale: |
  HLD_PROPOSED_001 requires a google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member (or _binding)
  granting the AI Platform service agent access to the CMEK key, but the
  grant and the dataset both reference the same key without either
  referencing the other, so Terraform treats them as parallel siblings and
  may create the dataset before the IAM grant propagates. This produces a
  "Cloud KMS permission denied" error on first apply that only resolves on
  retry. Same requires_ordered_companion shape as HLD_GCP_465 and HLD_GCP_494.
remediation: |
  Add depends_on = [google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.<name>] to the
  google_vertex_ai_dataset resource so that Terraform always applies the IAM
  grant before attempting to create the dataset.
resources:
  google_vertex_ai_dataset:
    requires_ordered_companion:
      type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
      match:
        source_path: encryption_spec.kms_key_name
        companion_path: crypto_key_id
      order: depends_on
